From 9597ab9a8296ab337e6820f8a717ff621078b632 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mikko Perttunen <mperttunen@nvidia.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 15:50:42 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] memory: tegra124-emc: Fix dll_change check

The code checking whether the specified memory timing enables DLL
in the EMRS register was reversed. DLL is enabled if bit A0 is low.
Fix the check.

Fixes: 73a7f0a90641 ("memory: tegra: Add EMC (external memory controller) driver")
Signed-off-by: Mikko Perttunen <mperttunen@nvidia.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260126-fix-emc-dllchange-v1-1-47ad3bb63262@nvidia.com
Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzk@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/memory/tegra/tegra124-emc.c b/drivers/memory/tegra/tegra124-emc.c
index ff26815e51f1..5cfbc169c5f9 100644
--- a/drivers/memory/tegra/tegra124-emc.c
+++ b/drivers/memory/tegra/tegra124-emc.c
@@ -608,7 +608,7 @@ static int tegra124_emc_prepare_timing_change(struct tegra_emc *emc,
 
 	if ((last->emc_mode_1 & 0x1) == (timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))
 		dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_NONE;
-	else if (timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1)
+	else if (!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))
 		dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_ON;
 	else
 		dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_OFF;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a bug in the `tegra124_emc_prepare_timing_change` function within `drivers/memory/tegra/tegra124-emc.c`. The issue is a reversed condition when checking whether the memory timing enables the DLL (Delay-Locked Loop) via the EMRS register.

### Modification in the File

- **File**: `drivers/memory/tegra/tegra124-emc.c`
- **Change**: In line 611, the condition `if (timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1)` was replaced with `if (!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))`.
- **Effect**: Previously, the code incorrectly set `dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_ON` when the EMRS register’s bit A0 was set (value 1). Actually, DLL is enabled when bit A0 is **low** (value 0). The fix corrects this logic so that `DLL_CHANGE_ON` is assigned when bit A0 is 0, and `DLL_CHANGE_OFF` when it is 1.

### Relationship

The patch addresses a logic error that caused the driver to misinterpret the DLL enable state derived from the EMRS register. The original condition was inverted, leading to incorrect behavior during memory timing changes. The fix aligns the code with the hardware specification, ensuring proper DLL state transitions.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
else if (timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1)

Reason:
The hardware specification states that DLL is enabled when bit A0 (bit 0) of the EMRS register is low (0), not high (1). The original code incorrectly set `dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_ON` when the bit was high, causing improper DLL state transitions during timing changes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
else if (!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))

Reason:
The fix inverts the condition so that `dll_change = DLL_CHANGE_ON` is set only when bit 0 is low, matching the hardware requirement. This ensures correct DLL enable/disable behavior during memory timing changes.

The bug was due to an inverted logical condition in the tegra124_emc_prepare_timing_change function. The EMRS register's bit A0 (bit 0) indicates that DLL is enabled when the bit is low (0), not high (1). The correct logic requires checking `if (!(timing->emc_mode_1 & 0x1))` to set `DLL_CHANGE_ON` when bit A0 is low, matching the hardware specification. This misalignment caused improper DLL state transitions during memory timing changes.
